title: 送杜少府之任蜀州
titlePy: Sòng Dù Shàofǔ Zhī Rèn Shǔzhōu
titleEn: Seeing Off Vice-Magistrate Du to His Post in Shuzhou
author: 王勃
intro: A farewell poem that refuses to be sad: “As long as I have a true friend somewhere within the seas, the ends of the earth are like next door.” Written by a poet barely out of his teens.
analysis: 王勃在长安送朋友杜少府去四川做官。前两句写送别的地点和远方：三秦护卫着长安城，透过风烟遥望朋友要去的蜀地五津。一近一远，把两地连起来。三、四句说：我和你一样，都是离开家乡在外做官的人，离别的心情彼此都懂。五、六句是全诗最有名的两句：只要四海之内有知心朋友，就算远在天边，也像住在隔壁一样。这两句把空间的距离变成了心灵的贴近，打破了送别诗一般的伤感，今天还常被写在给远方朋友的信和卡片上。最后两句劝朋友：不要在分别的路口，像小儿女一样哭得泪水湿透手巾。整首诗开阔、乐观，一改离别诗哭哭啼啼的调子。
analysisEn: Wang Bo is in Chang’an seeing off a friend named Du, who is going to take up a minor post in Sichuan. The opening couplet joins the two places: the capital, guarded by the land of Three Qin, and far away through wind and haze, the Five Fords of Shu where Du is heading. Then: “We share the same feeling at parting — we are both men far from home, serving as officials.” The third couplet is why the poem is loved: “As long as there is a true friend within the four seas, the ends of the earth are like next door.” Physical distance becomes closeness of heart, and the usual tearful mood of farewell poems is turned upside down. Chinese people still write these lines in cards and messages to friends abroad. The ending gently tells his friend not to stand at the fork in the road and wet their handkerchiefs with tears like young boys and girls. The whole poem is broad-minded and hopeful, a very different note from most Tang farewells.
background: Wang Bo (c. 650–676) was a child prodigy, one of the “Four Talents of the Early Tang”. He wrote this as a young man in Chang’an, probably still in his teens or early twenties; he drowned crossing the sea at about 26.
pronunciation: 少府 shào fǔ（官名，不读 shǎo）；城阙 què；宦游 huàn yóu；无为 wú wéi（不要，不读 wèi）；歧路 qí lù；沾巾 zhān jīn。
version: 采用通行教材版本。题目一作《送杜少府之任蜀川》，“风烟望五津”一作“风烟望五川”，网站按教材作“蜀州”“五津”。

lines.lit: The city towers are guarded by the Three Qin;
lines.en: The capital stands guarded by the land of Qin;

lines.lit: through wind and mist I gaze toward the Five Fords.
lines.en: through wind and haze I look toward the fords of Shu.

lines.lit: The feeling of parting I share with you —
lines.en: You and I feel this parting the same way:

lines.lit: we are both men travelling for office.
lines.en: we are both far from home, serving away.

lines.lit: Within the seas there remains a true friend;
lines.en: If a true friend lives anywhere within the seas,

lines.lit: the edge of the sky is like next door.
lines.en: the ends of the earth are just next door.

lines.lit: Let us not, at the forking road,
lines.en: So let’s not stand here where the road divides

lines.lit: like boys and girls together wet our scarves.
lines.en: wetting our sleeves with tears like children.

words.en: to go to take up a post
words.note: 之：去、到；任：职位，现代汉语“上任”“赴任”。

words.en: city towers — i.e. the capital Chang’an
the Three Qin — the area around Chang’an (today’s Shaanxi)
words.note: 今天“三秦大地”仍指陕西。

words.en: the Five Fords on the Min River in Sichuan
to travel away from home as an official
within the four seas — the whole country, the world
words.note: 古人认为中国四面环海。今天“海内外”。

words.en: a true friend who understands you
words.note: 今天仍常用，如“知己朋友”。

words.en: the edge of the sky; the ends of the earth

words.note: 古义“不要”；今天“无为”多指道家的“无为而治”。

words.en: fork in the road — where friends part
words.note: 今天“误入歧途”“歧路”多指错误的路。

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 风烟弥漫，望不到远方的蜀地，写出两地相隔的遥远。
imagery.en: Wind and haze blur the view toward distant Shu — a measure of how far apart the friends will be.

imagery.name: 海
imagery.zh: “海内”指整个天下：天下再大，有知己就不觉得远。
imagery.en: “Within the seas” means the whole world — however big it is, a true friend makes it small.

imagery.name: 歧路
imagery.zh: 分岔的路口是朋友分手的地方，诗人劝朋友不要在这里流泪。
imagery.en: The fork in the road is where friends part — and where the poet asks his friend not to cry.
